title: $200 Bonus with Orange One Low Credit Card after Spending $500 in 3 Months ($48 Annual Fee / $0 with Orange Adv home loan) @ ING
body:
Deal: $200 Bonus with Orange One Low Credit Card after Spending $500 in 3 Months ($48 Annual Fee / $0 with Orange Adv home loan) @ ING

[Checkmate3023] Man the Cerdit card churning is so dead if this is what ING bank is offering
[cski] 40% cashback to $500 spend seems generous to me
[Aureus] Plus $48 fee. Good offer for those who don't have to pay the fee
[spaceflight] Talk about high expectations when minimum 30.4% cashback is a bad offer!
[idm] Do you consider a hard credit check for $150 return a good deal?
[Hereforthegoods] obviously this isn't the best churn card in the world. But it can be a pretty reasonable deal if you're just looking for a no frills credit product. Besides, what are you expecting for a low fees CC?
[Dyl] This is one of the best deals I’ve seen for churning in ages…
[hasher22] Note
ING does NOT allow credit card increases/decreases. When you sign up, that's your card until cancelled.
I have a 2k limit and wanted a 3k limit, they said I have to cancel the card first THEN sign up to a new credit card with a new limit. But I argued what happens if I get declined and I need my CC as I pay it off the monthly balance in full. They pretty much said, bad luck, cancel the card first and try sign up with a higher limit.
Effectively, you will need to submit all documents again, credit check and they will treat you as a new customer and will not even consider your history with ING. I said does my monthly incoming salary count as evidence for the last 8+ years and paying my CC off monthly in full count as evidence. HE SAID NO… WTF
You cannot have more than 1 CC on the account.
Considering this card was $0 p.a and they slugged the year fee…. for what….
You also need an everyday account and/or a savings account to pay off the balance. You can't pay it off from an external source.
This is just a bait deal, to get ~$150 back (after CC fee) is really mediocre considering you have to open other accounts, transfer money and pay off the balance if you can be bothered.
[Dyl] Your credit report will show your positive repayment history, you’ll likely get accepted.
It’s common to do a new credit check when providing a higher limit, though a bit unusual they make you reapply.
[linkser] Not useful for churning but I appreciate they don't charge international transaction fees which otherwise a lot of other ccs with points do.
[Dyl] It’s a decent churn considering even people on disability pension can likely access it if they have no other lines of credit open.
Personally I still have $19,000 open from when I worked so wouldn’t be eligible.
